page: Hetzner Cloud cx23 is an entry-level virtual server belonging to the Cost Optimized family. Built on QEMU virtualization, it utilizes an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core. The processor includes 32 KB L1d, 4 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache, with instruction set support for AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and bit manipulation primitives like BMI2 and ADX. It provides 4.0 GB of RAM, equating to roughly 1.95 GB of memory per core, paired with a bundled 40 GB NVMe SSD for local storage. Dedicated hardware accelerators are not included, and it does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations position the cx23 in the lower tier across processing and memory tests. The instance registered a Geekbench single-core score of 713.0 and a multi-core score of 1233.0, reflecting its shared 2.0 GHz core allocation. Stress-ng returned 1028.88 on single-core and 2016.78 on multi-core operations. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 149.36 GB/sec for small cached reads, dropping to 20.91 GB/sec for uncached read blocks and 16.93 GB/sec for uncached writes. Application-specific benchmarks show static web serving throughput of 1.77 GB/sec, Redis SET throughput at 2.52 million operations per second, and 52.23 tokens per second text generation on a lightweight 135M parameter LLM.

The shared-CPU provisioning model and modest 4.0 GB memory capacity reflect a budget-conscious resource profile designed for low-demand hosting. While NVMe storage offers responsive local disk operations, the conservative compute and memory limits restrict high-throughput concurrency or heavy analytical queries. Hetzner Cloud cx23 is best suited for small-scale web serving, light background workers, development and testing environments, low-traffic static websites, and lightweight microservices that operate within modest computational constraints.

It contains no GPU hardware and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.
